subject.title: Browser backend plugin interface (support third-party drivers via MCP/custom adapter)

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic browser backend Plugin SDK/registry seam for third-party drivers, or keep browser backends limited to narrow first-party profile drivers for now?
rationale: The requested seam is public API plus a browser-control security boundary, so automation cannot safely choose the long-term contract by widening enums or landing a one-off driver.

options.title: Design generic SDK registry
options.body: Add a versioned backend contract, registry-owned driver ids, config/schema/client/runtime routing, docs, and security tests before accepting third-party adapters.

options.title: Limit to first-party drivers
options.body: Handle Browserbase, My Browser, and relay needs as individual built-in or bundled-plugin drivers without exposing a generic third-party contract yet.

options.title: Defer until demand PRs settle
options.body: Keep this issue open while narrower Browserbase, My Browser, relay, and sandbox-backend work clarifies the minimum safe registration API.

recommendation.title: Design generic SDK registry
recommendation.body: Add a versioned backend contract, registry-owned driver ids, config/schema/client/runtime routing, docs, and security tests before accepting third-party adapters.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the strongest recent history on the browser driver migration and profile-driver seam.
